title: At her place
goal: Add case endings after his, her and their: evinde, arabasına, kapısını.

intro.text: After the third-person possessive, a case ending takes an extra n: *evi* → *evinde* (at his house), *arabası* → *arabasına* (into her car), *kapısı* → *kapısını* (its door, as an object). The other persons don't: *evimde*, *arabamıza*.

vocab.en: to close, to shut; to turn off

exercises.question: How do you say **at Ayşe's house**?

why.1: After the third-person *-i*, the locative needs an n: *evinde*.
why.2: *Evde* drops the possessive. Ayşe's house is *evi*, so: *evinde*.
why.3: The last vowel is i, a front vowel: *-de*.

reject.why: After the third-person possessive, the buffer is n, not y: *arabasına*.
The possessive *-sı* needs an n before the dative: *arabasına*.

exercises.explain: *Binmek* takes the dative, and after *-sı* the dative is *-na*: *arabasına*.

exercises.prompt: She lives in her mother's house.

reject.why: The house is her mother's, *annesinin evi*, so the locative is *evinde*.
After *evi*, the locative takes an n: *evinde*.

exercises.label: *ev* + possessive + locative: in my house, in your house…
exercises.explain: Only the third person adds an n: *ev-i-n-de*, *ev-leri-n-de*. The second person, *ev-in-de*, happens to read the same.

exercises.en: We're staying at her mother's house.

exercises.explain: *kapı* + *s* + *-ı* (her door), then n + *-ı* for the accusative: *kapısını*.

accept: Ayşe is looking for her key.

exercises.prompt: We are sitting in our neighbour's garden.

exercises.en: Elif is going to Selin's house.
exercises.explain: After *evi* (her house), the dative takes an n: *evine*.

exercises.prompt: The pharmacy is on the corner of the street.

reject.why: It's the street's corner, *sokağın köşesi*, so the locative is *köşesinde*.
Before a vowel the k of *sokak* softens: *sokağın*.

exercises.question: *Evinde* can mean two things. Which?
options: in your house, or in his house
in my house, or in your house
in the house, or in his house
exercises.explain: *Ev-in-de* (your house) and *ev-i-n-de* (his house) read the same; *senin* or *onun* tells them apart.

accept: My brother is turning off the light in his room.
My sister is turning off the light in her room.
My [brother|sister|sibling] is turning the light off in [his|her|their] room.
My [brother|sister|sibling] is switching [off the light|the light off] in [his|her|their] room.
My sibling is turning off the light in [his|her|their] room.
